# A clockless noisy classical register and buffered copy

29 October 2026. This is a restricted CLASSICAL operation with a fully
specified asynchronous controller and a sustained-noise bound. It is not a
decoder for the programme's recursive quantum code. The interaction graph
is an explicitly admitted expander, rather than an implicitly free
three-dimensional wiring network. No noiseless persistent bit, synchronizing
clock, causal fault-label assumption, or quiet interval is used.

## 1. Primitive and exact input contract

Let P be the symmetric transition matrix of a regular undirected multigraph
on n sites, including multiplicities and loops, with uniform stationary
law. Suppose

    ||P-Pi||_(2->2) <= s,   Pi=11^T/n.

Fix an integer ell. Put W=P^ell and assume

    3(1/64+s^(2ell)) <= 1/8.                              (1)

There is one physical classical bit per site. Each site has an independent
Poisson update clock of a possibly unknown, fixed rate r_i in [15/16,17/16].
The nominal rate is1; this interval allows a stated static calibration
error without a perfect global timing signal. At its update, draw THREE independent
ell-step P walks starting at that site, read their three endpoint bits,
and replace the site's bit by their majority. Sampling is with replacement;
the target and sampled sites may coincide. Every fixed draw gives a monotone,
self-dual Boolean map. There is no state besides these n bits.

Unknown faults occur on a fixed catalogue of nonempty supports X, |X|<=q,
at independent state-independent Poisson rates k_X. They are independent of
nominal clocks and walk coins. At a fault, the replacement of the bits on X
is ARBITRARY. In particular it may depend on the initial bit, the entire
past, all future nominal clocks/coins and all other fault locations. Require

    max_i sum_(X containing i) k_X <= lambda,
    lambda <= 1/[1024(2^q-1)].                            (2)

Thus Lambda=sum_X k_X<=n lambda. The theorem is pathwise over all supported
replacement labels; the maximum is INSIDE expectation over the clocks,
coins and unlabelled fault support process. A state-dependent unknown point
process is not silently substituted for this input.

The classical bit b to be retained is encoded as all b, with at most
m0<=floor(n/256) initially incorrect bits. The locations are arbitrary,
but the initial configuration is independent of future clocks

source_excerpts.text:
# Completed restricted operation; native quantum gate still open

The construction gives a retained CLASSICAL bit and an always-running
buffered copy into an arbitrary noisy destination. Both use one noisy bit
per site and fixed local Poisson channels, with no persistent clock or
history tape. The proof controls failure at ANY time in the interval and
admits future-dependent supported fault labels. It does not replace the
desired quantum syndrome decoder by an ideal classical register.

The load-bearing step is monotonicity: for each retained value, setting
every fault-touched bit to the WRONG value is a single pathwise worst
trajectory. That trajectory is Markov, so the subsequent drift/exponential
proof has a legitimate filtration. A direct Markov argument for the
original future-dependent fault labels would be invalid.

For n bits on the admitted graph and q-bit fault supports, the sufficient
conditions are initial errors<=n/256, per-bit Poisson fault incidence
lambda<=1/[1024(2^q-1)], and clock rates in[15/16,17/16]. The all-time
register failure upper is

    2^q n(1+lambda) T exp(-n/256).

The copy has an explicit initialization-forgetting term and exponential
excursion term in PROOF(8). A read-q bound supplies simultaneous all-time
failure bounds for many separate register/copy pairs, including fault
streams shared by up to q pairs. Arbitrary inter-pair feedback is excluded.

## Actually constructed

The exact n=65536, q=1 output uses the standard explicit eight-incidence
Margulis graph, three length16 walks per attempt, 144 fair bits and at most
four accessed data bits per update. Restoring/copy graph ranges are16/17.
The full524288-incidence graph catalogue (2097152bytes) was emitted and
checked. Its eight directional permutations and every inverse identity
passed. The named all-moduli spectral theorem is an ordinary imported
premise, not a numerically fitted eigenvalue.

At lambda=1/1024, with up to256 source errors, T=2^128 and copy latency256,
REGISTER_CONTRACT.json gives a total buffered-copy failure upper

    3.855621470697103e-34   (decimal diagnostic of an EXACT rational bound).

This is a compiled theorem receiver, not an executed long-time memory
experiment. No trajectory or new quantum-code fixture was generated.
The final graph/contract compilation took0.242976s and28.74MB peak RSS;
the earlier exact-rate-only compilation took0.232868s.
